mjolnir — code verification

The Notary for the AI-Code Era

AI writes the code. Someone has to guarantee it. Nobody does. We do — provably.

Value proposition

For the engineering leader: "Every piece of code that ships — whether written by your team or generated by AI — comes with a proof of the safety claims that matter, and the proof is re-checkable by anyone, forever. Today's review process is 'trust the engineer, hope the tests cover it'. We replace that with a verdict that cannot be fooled, at one command per release."

For the investor: "AI now writes the code that runs hospitals, cars, and factories. Regulation (FDA, EU AI Act, ISO 26262) demands proof, not model confidence. There is no certification layer for AI-generated code. We are that layer: deterministic math decides, AI only suggests — so our approvals can't be hallucinated, and every rejection comes with the failing input attached."

Impact — what measurably changes

Review cost collapses. Managers review signed patterns — 15 decisions covered 736 claims in our live demo — instead of thousands of items. Each review is one-time, permanent, compounding.

Audit cost drops. The release artifact is a bundle: claims + proof steps + independent re-check + signatures. An auditor re-verifies with one small program — no access to your models, no "re-run the CI and pray".

AI-code velocity becomes safe velocity. Generated code gets three outcomes: proven (ship, artifact attached), provably broken (repaired with the failing input — a counterexample, not a vague score), or honestly blocked. The repair loop is closed: failing example → regenerate → re-check.

Liability becomes assignable. "The AI wrote it and tests passed" is indefensible in court. A signed, tamper-evident certificate chain per deployed unit is the defense regulators and insurers will require — that's the purchase order.

The moat — five layers
1
Neurosymbolic architecture. Program synthesis from frozen latent space with an exact, traceable disposal layer — propose/dispose separated, every proof step audited. The equations are public; the architecture that makes them safe together is the part that took years of failures to assemble. A competitor can copy the math in a week; they cannot copy the reasons it is wired this way — those live in our test set.
2
Built-in soundness. Zero false approvals — enforced by design and backed by the live attack battery (7/7 falsified claims caught in the current report). Competitors can't make that claim falsifiable, which means they can't lose it — and therefore can't win the regulated deal.
3
Compounding registry. Mined claims + human-confirmed patterns accumulate across repos and customers. Every new repo makes the registry stronger; every confirmation transfers — with per-target validation — to the next. Network effects on safety knowledge: the more it is used, the fewer decisions remain unmade.
4
Regression discipline. A 63-case capability test set, each with an adversarial twin, pins the checker's behavior. The soundness bugs we caught — false rejections, stale-fact leaks, pattern collapse — were each caught by this test set. A competitor must rebuild years of exactly this discipline; it is the moat's insurance policy.
5
Demonstrated scalability + near-zero parameter cost. 272,000 lines of real code scanned in under 3 seconds — 3,749 claims with full source provenance, on a laptop, no GPU. And the trainable parameter count is effectively zero: the neural encoder is frozen and only ever proposes. No training runs, no GPU fleet, no silent model drift — the deciding core is deterministic algebra, so verdicts reproduce byte-for-byte and unit economics are near-zero. The upgrade path stays open: when we train our own domain encoder, it drops into the proposer slot — better suggestions, higher coverage — while the soundness guarantees stay untouched, because the gate never trusted the model in the first place.
The honest boundary — stated before it's asked

Coverage on arbitrary real repos is low today and reported as-is. The climb is scheduled, not speculative: each step is a bounded piece of engineering with a predicted, measured delta — the 94% of claims currently "needs more evidence" become eligible through test-harvest and the premise machinery already built. We sell verdict quality first (regulated, high-stakes deployments where correctness per claim beats coverage per repo); the coverage climb is the expansion revenue.
